item.text:
**6B.7 Research Note**

**Verdict:** mostly no. Putin’s 2024 record includes some universal or need-based welfare measures that were not explicitly conditioned on loyalty. But there is strong evidence that welfare, jobs, housing, benefits, and related administrative controls were also used as tools of pressure, punishment, and exclusion, especially in occupied areas, against migrants, and against dissenters.

| Stance | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Support | [Program of state guarantees for free medical care, 2024-2026](https://government.ru/docs/all/151778/) | Government of Russia | 2024-01-09 | https://government.ru/docs/all/151778/ | Russia kept a universal free-medical-care program in force, including high-tech and specialized treatment. This is a need-based welfare measure rather than an obvious loyalty test. | 6B.7; 6B.2; 6B.6 |
| Support | [Nationwide family support for large families](https://government.ru/en/news/50700/) | Government of Russia | 2024-01-25 | https://government.ru/en/news/50700/ | Parents with three or more children were promised equal support throughout the country, regardless of region. That is a broad entitlement, not obviously tied to political loyalty. | 6B.7; 6B.2; 6B.3 |
| Support | [Caregiver allowance for disabled children kept while working](https://government.ru/news/50822/) | Government of Russia | 2024-02-08 | https://government.ru/news/50822/ | Caregivers of disabled children could keep the monthly allowance even if they took part-time work. This looks like targeted social support, not political punishment. | 6B.7; 6B.2; 6B.3 |
| Support | [Rehabilitation support for children with disabilities expanded](https://government.ru/docs/53649/) | Government of Russia | 2024-12-09 | https://government.ru/docs/53649/ | The rehab pilot expanded from 3 to 38 regions and covered rehab, lodging, meals, and travel costs. This is welfare expansion with no explicit loyalty condition. | 6B.7; 6B.2; 6B.3; 6B.6 |
| Support | [Full-scale benefit administration in occupied/new regions](https://sfr.gov.ru/en/press_center/~2024/12/18/276536) | Social Fund of Russia | 2024-12-18 | https://sfr.gov.ru/en/press_center/~2024/12/18/276536 | The Social Fund reported pensions, child benefits, disability support, sick-leave digitization, and health-worker payments in occupied/new regions. This shows benefits being administered, though inside a war/occupation framework. | 6B.7; 6B.2; 6B.3; 6B.4; 6B.6 |
| Against | [UN report details “climate of fear” in occupied areas](https://ukraine.un.org/en/264055-un-report-details-%E2%80%98climate-fear%E2%80%99-occupied-areas-ukraine-russian-federation-moves-cement) | United Nations in Ukraine | 2024-03-20 | https://ukraine.un.org/en/264055-un-report-details-%E2%80%98climate-fear%E2%80%99-occupied-areas-ukraine-russian-federation-moves-cement | The UN said residents who refused Russian passports were progressively denied public-sector jobs, healthcare, and social-security benefits. That is direct use of welfare and employment as coercive tools. | 6B.7; 6B.2; 6B.3 |
| Against | [Russia to curb income of “foreign agents” and those who leave](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-to-curb-income-of-foreign-agents-and-those-who-leave-lawmaker-says-3707363) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-11-07 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-to-curb-income-of-foreign-agents-and-those-who-leave-lawmaker-says-3707363 | Reuters reported plans to tighten income rules for “foreign agents” and people who criticize Russia after leaving. That is punitive use of livelihood rules against dissent. | 6B.7; 6B.1; 6B.3 |
| Against | [Russia expands extremist listing grounds and Rosfinmonitoring access](https://tass.ru/obschestvo/22793553) | TASS | 2024-12-28 | https://tass.ru/obschestvo/22793553 | Putin signed a law expanding extremist/terrorist listing grounds and giving Rosfinmonitoring access to the bank data of people financing extremism. That expands financial punishment and surveillance. | 6B.7; 6B.1; 6B.3 |
| Against | [After Crocus, Russia punishes Tajik migrants](https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-punishes-tajik-migrants-deportations-entry-moscow-terror-attack/32891458.html) | RFE/RL | 2024-04-04 | https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-punishes-tajik-migrants-deportations-entry-moscow-terror-attack/32891458.html | Police raids, entry denials, deportations, and aggressive questioning looked like collective punishment of a vulnerable migrant group. That is a clear punitive use of state power against livelihood and mobility. | 6B.7; 6B.3; 6B.6 |
| Against | [More than 400 detained at Navalny memorials and rallies](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/2/17/more-than-100-detained-at-navalny-memorials-in-russia-rights-group) | Al Jazeera | 2024-02-17 | https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/2/17/more-than-100-detained-at-navalny-memorials-in-russia-rights-group | More than 400 people were detained at Navalny memorials and rallies, showing retaliation against dissent rather than neutral treatment of citizens seeking public expression. | 6B.7; 6B.1 |

**Search gap:** I found a few universal or need-based welfare measures, but very little evidence that Putin systematically avoided using welfare and benefits as political tools. The clearest 2024 record points the other way: occupation-linked denial of services, punitive migrant controls, financial restrictions on critics, and broad coercive administration of access and benefits.
